items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I've never met Benny Carter personally, but I've always admired him since I first heard him back in the Thirties.

ctx.x: But anyway, in the rhythm section was Tommy Potter on bass. The guitarist... The only guy that I know that could create almost exactly like Freddie Greene... Carney Wainwright was the guitar player. And I was the pianist, of course.

And during the wartime situation, all musicians were hard to find. We were fortunate to get these people. We had hoped to have either Max Roach or Shadow Wilson with the band, but somebody had scooped both of them up. I think Max Roach was with Benny Carter at that particular time, and I don't know exactly what Shadow was doing. I know a little later he was with the Basie band. I don't know whether he was with Basie or not when the band started. But I know he wasn't available. I think he might have been in the…

But after trying to get drummers, we couldn't... So there was a fellow, and I don't know his name because I never really knew what his name was. He was a very nice guy. He was a White fellow. And he came to play drums with the band.
